nodes.name: Zgok 01
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Two Z'Goks face one porcelain teapot, one paper roll, and six meters of eager ribbon.{pause}The gift must reach their neighbor's birthday party in exactly one hour.{pause}Red Z'Gok has promised a professional parcel with square corners and tasteful restraint.{pause}Blue Z'Gok has brought a first-aid kit specifically for the paper.

nodes.name: Zgok 02
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Claws are precision instruments used for delicate work under difficult conditions.{pause}Blue points out that last year's card still has four perfectly round puncture marks.{pause}Red calls those ventilation features and places the teapot at the paper's center.{pause}The teapot looks fragile, round, and unconvinced by the briefing.

nodes.name: Zgok 03
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: We begin by measuring twice, cutting once, and not rotating our arms near the ribbon.{pause}Red measures the teapot from spout to handle while Blue records every number.{pause}They forget to include height, then measure again with greater professional seriousness.{pause}The paper roll quietly curls itself back up whenever neither robot is looking.

nodes.name: Zgok 04
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Blue holds one end of the paper; Red unrolls the other across the living-room floor.{pause}The roll passes under a chair, around a table leg, and into the hallway.{pause}When they finally stop it, they have measured enough paper for a small canoe.{pause}Red says extra coverage is a sign of care, not a units error.

nodes.name: Zgok 05
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: The first cut will be straight, controlled, and free from all card-related ventilation.{pause}Red lowers one claw tip and slices a perfect line through paper, rug, and silence.{pause}Blue lifts the rug edge; the cut stopped one thread before becoming a household discussion.{pause}They move the project onto the table and place the first-aid kit beside the rug.

nodes.name: Zgok 06
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Tape is safer than cutting because tape cannot make holes in the furniture.{pause}Blue peels a strip, which sticks to one claw before reaching the paper.{pause}The second claw attempts rescue and becomes attached to the first at a thoughtful angle.{pause}Red offers help, then wisely waits until Blue has finished expressing several concerns.

nodes.name: Zgok 07
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Red braces the tape roll while Blue walks backward to free the trapped strip.{pause}The tape stretches across the room, catches a lamp cord, and rings a tiny bell ornament.{pause}Both Z'Goks freeze; the teapot remains unharmed and somehow looks smug.{pause}They cut the strip with kitchen scissors held between both sets of claws.

nodes.name: Zgok 08
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: A simple box would solve the round shape, exposed spout, and judgmental handle.{pause}Blue presents three boxes: one too small, one too flat, and one labeled winter boots.{pause}The boot box fits the teapot but leaves enough room for it to begin a second life.{pause}They add two towels as padding and apologize to the towels for the temporary assignment.

nodes.name: Zgok 09
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: We can practice folds on scrap paper or build a cardboard guide for the claws.{pause}Practice may waste paper; a guide may become permanently attached to one of us.{pause}Red says both risks are manageable and the clock says forty-two minutes remain.{pause}They choose a first method while the ribbon watches from the chair like a coiled spectator.

nodes.name: Zgok 10
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The table is cleared except for the padded box, paper, tape, ribbon, and emergency snacks.{pause}Red reviews the desired result: protected teapot, clean folds, visible birthday spirit.{pause}Blue adds a fourth goal involving both robots leaving the room independently.{pause}The teapot receives a towel hood so it does not have to watch the experiment.

nodes.name: Zgok Practice 1
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: They practice valley folds, corner folds, and one shape that resembles a worried fish.{pause}Blue learns to press paper with the flat side of a claw instead of the point.{pause}Red makes a tiny paper hat and places it on the tape dispenser for morale.{pause}The dispenser looks experienced now, which is useful because both robots need supervision.

nodes.name: Zgok Practice 2
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Practice improves control, though each fold still includes a small circular signature.{pause}They cover the holes with star stickers and declare a new decorative technique.{pause}Blue folds a clean corner on the third attempt and receives the paper hat.{pause}The scraps become gift tags, making the exercise waste-free and suspiciously charming.

nodes.name: Zgok Guide 1
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Blue cuts cardboard sleeves that slide over each claw like square training shoes.{pause}Red tests one and loses all ability to pick up anything narrower than a sandwich.{pause}The sleeves press broad folds beautifully but bump together whenever both arms move.{pause}They name the movement Formal Cardboard Applause and promise not to demonstrate it at parties.

nodes.name: Zgok Guide 2
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: The guide prevents punctures, protects the table, and makes tape handling nearly{pause}impossible.{pause}Red traps one strip between two cardboard sleeves and carries it like a ceremonial banner.{pause}Blue removes a sleeve for precision, then replaces it before the claw finds the rug.{pause}Together they develop a rhythm: broad press, bare-claw tape, immediate sleeve return.

nodes.name: Zgok 11
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Tape Trouble returns as the real sheet of paper finally meets the boot box.{pause}Practice folds or cardboard guides, the claws now move with visible care and slower{pause}confidence.{pause}Red centers the box while Blue brings the long edges together above it.{pause}For one shining moment, the paper fits, the corners align, and nobody is attached.

nodes.name: Zgok 12
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Hold that position while I prepare one exact strip of tape, no longer than necessary.{pause}Red pulls the strip; the dispenser slides; Blue catches it with an elbow.{pause}The strip lands across the seam and also across Red's left forearm.{pause}Red calls this temporary stabilization and asks Blue not to photograph it.

nodes.name: Zgok 13
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Blue frees Red by rotating the paper roll instead of pulling on the stuck arm.{pause}The idea works, but it rolls the entire parcel one full turn across the table.{pause}A towel shifts inside, and the teapot gives one tiny porcelain clink.{pause}Both Z'Goks stop breathing despite neither requiring the habit.

nodes.name: Zgok 14
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They open one end and inspect the teapot beneath its towel hood.{pause}It is safe, centered, and apparently unaware of how close the room came to panic.{pause}Blue adds a rolled washcloth beside the spout and one beside the handle.{pause}Red calls the arrangement a suspension cradle and closes the end with quieter claws.

nodes.name: Zgok 15
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: The side folds must meet like two doors, not like waves striking a sea wall.{pause}Blue folds the lower flap; Red folds the upper; their cardboard sleeves bump once.{pause}Formal Cardboard Applause echoes through the room, startling the tiny bell ornament.{pause}They laugh, lose the fold, and make it again without blaming the paper.

nodes.name: Zgok 16
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: We have nineteen minutes, one wrapped box, and a seam that resembles a mountain range.{pause}Red smooths the high points while Blue applies short tape bridges between them.{pause}The star stickers cover four claw signatures and one place that never had a hole.{pause}The parcel now looks handmade rather than attacked, which counts as major progress.

nodes.name: Zgok 17
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They write a card using a marker strapped between two claw tips with ribbon.{pause}Red writes HAPPY; Blue steadies the marker for BIRTHDAY; both attempt the final exclamation point.{pause}The dot becomes a red circle large enough to be interpreted as a seal.{pause}They place the paper hat on the card and decide the message is complete.

nodes.name: Zgok 18
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: The ribbon should cross beneath the box, meet above it, and remain free of furniture.{pause}Blue threads one end under while Red lifts the parcel by exactly two centimeters.{pause}The ribbon catches a towel corner inside the loose end flap and refuses to move.{pause}They reopen the flap, free it, and discover the teapot still sitting patiently.

nodes.name: Zgok 19
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: The teapot has survived measuring, rolling, inspection, applause, and our card lettering.{pause}Red says the gift deserves a final wrapping method equal to that endurance.{pause}Blue says it deserves arrival before the candles are lit and checks the clock.{pause}Twelve minutes remain, enough for either caution or one impressive mistake.

nodes.name: Zgok 20
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Claw and Ribbon returns as Red places both ribbon ends on the tabletop.{pause}He remembers last year's ventilated card and this year's nearly cut rug.{pause}Blue remembers the clean corner, the rescued parcel, and Formal Cardboard Applause.{pause}They agree that improvement can still look funny while it is happening.{pause}The paper hat leans on the dispenser, proof that mistakes can become decorations.{pause}Red thanks Blue for bringing a first-aid kit for paper and patience for him.{pause}Blue says both supplies were necessary, though only the patience roll is nearly empty.

nodes.name: Zgok 21
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: The main tape tune resumes while they remove every unnecessary strip from their claws.{pause}One strip has collected dust, thread, and the missing sticker shaped like a moon.{pause}Blue turns it into a final gift tag rather than letting it touch the parcel.{pause}The tag reads FROM BOTH OF US, although the moon covers most of BOTH.

nodes.name: Zgok 22
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: A neighbor knocks to ask whether they are ready, then sees the ribbon across the room.{pause}Red answers yes with the specific confidence of someone who has not tied the bow.{pause}The neighbor offers two oven mitts and says they helped with last winter's cookies.{pause}Blue accepts them as specialized soft-hand equipment with a proven domestic record.

nodes.name: Zgok 23
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The mitts slide over Red's claw tips, turning each arm into a padded red paddle.{pause}He can press paper without punctures but cannot grip the narrow ribbon ends.{pause}Blue discovers that rotating forearms can wind ribbon without pinching it at all.{pause}Two final methods now sit on the table, equally useful and equally dangerous to dignity.

nodes.name: Zgok 24
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Mitts allow slow folds, broad padding, and maximum protection around every corner.{pause}A ribbon spin creates a large bow quickly but could involve nearby chairs.{pause}The clock shows eight minutes; the party music is audible through the shared wall.{pause}Blue moves the lamp farther away before asking Red to choose.

nodes.name: Zgok 25
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Whatever we choose, the teapot is safe because we stopped and checked it twice.{pause}The paper is imperfect because four-clawed robots wrapped it for someone they like.{pause}Red places the paper hat beside the bow area as the parcel's official witness.{pause}Then both Z'Goks take their positions for the final operation.

nodes.name: Zgok 26
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: They rotate the parcel under the lamp and inspect every corner from claw height.{pause}One seam leans left, but the teapot cannot move when Blue performs a gentle shake test.{pause}The paper hat covers a tiny scrape where Red tried to pinch ribbon like string.{pause}Blue declares the flaw decorative, then records its location in case decoration spreads.{pause}For the first time all afternoon, both claws rest without gripping anything.

nodes.name: Zgok 27
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: They imagine the recipient opening the parcel at tomorrow's small kitchen party.{pause}Red practices saying this side up without pointing all four claws at the ceiling.{pause}Blue practices accepting thanks without listing the exact number of failed paper squares.{pause}The teapot matters, but so does arriving with a story that makes everyone laugh.{pause}A neat present and a funny present begin to sound like the same mission.

nodes.name: Zgok 28
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Oven mitts would soften every final press and protect the paper from sharp claw tips.{pause}A spinning ribbon pass would keep the claws apart and make the bow deliberately lively.{pause}Blue clears the table, moves the scissors away, and checks the teapot padding once more.{pause}Red places the practice scraps nearby as proof that careful work can still be ridiculous.{pause}They face the parcel together and choose how its last bright line should travel.

nodes.name: Zgok A1
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Soft hands, slow folds, and no heroic gestures until the package reaches the party.{pause}Red uses the mitts to press extra paper around the spout and handle sides.{pause}Blue tapes each padded corner with short strips learned during practice.{pause}The parcel grows rounder, softer, and increasingly similar to a festive weather balloon.

nodes.name: Zgok A2
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: They tie a small bow by looping ribbon around the oven mitt thumbs.{pause}When Red removes the mitts, the loops slide free without catching a claw.{pause}The paper hat sits at the bow's center, hiding the only untidy knot.{pause}Both earlier lessons pay off: broad pressure first, bare-claw precision only when necessary.

nodes.name: Zgok A3
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: At the party, the recipient unwraps six protective folds and discovers the padded boot{pause}box.{pause}Inside, the teapot emerges without a chip, scratch, or opinion about the journey.{pause}The towels become table runners, and the cardboard sleeves become cup holders.{pause}Everyone praises the enormous parcel before admitting they thought it contained a drum.

nodes.name: Zgok A4
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Red serves tea while wearing one oven mitt as the kitchen's official safety officer.{pause}Blue gives the paper hat to the teapot, which finally looks pleased with the project.{pause}The cut rug remains home, intact enough to never become a household discussion.{pause}Their new wrapping rule reads: MAXIMUM PROTECTION, MINIMUM UNPLANNED VENTILATION.

nodes.name: Zgok B1
nodes.speaker: Red Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Rotating forearms engage at the lowest speed while Blue feeds ribbon toward the parcel.{pause}One loop forms, then another, each broad enough to frame the entire boot box.{pause}The ribbon slips off a cardboard sleeve and sweeps around the nearest chair leg.{pause}Blue says keep going because stopping now would tighten everything in the wrong direction.

nodes.name: Zgok B2
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: Red reverses slowly; the chair slides closer, adding perfect tension to the final loop.{pause}Blue ties the center with the moon tag and clips the chair free using kitchen scissors.{pause}The bow springs open wider than the box, wider than the table, and nearly wider than pride.{pause}It is ridiculous, symmetrical, and completely untouched by claw holes.

nodes.name: Zgok B3
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They carry the parcel sideways through the hall because the bow will not fit forward.{pause}Party guests lift the ribbon loops overhead, turning delivery into an accidental parade.{pause}The recipient finds the safe teapot inside and wears one ribbon loop as a sash.{pause}Red calls the room-sized bow intentional; Blue produces the chair's signed release form.

nodes.name: Zgok B4
nodes.speaker: Blue Z'Gok
nodes.dialogue: After tea, the bow becomes party bunting stretched safely between two walls.{pause}The paper hat crowns the tape dispenser, which is invited as an honorary supervisor.{pause}Red and Blue dance Formal Cardboard Applause without wearing the cardboard sleeves.{pause}Their new wrapping rule reads: MOVE THE FURNITURE BEFORE THE RIBBON DEVELOPS AMBITION.
